candidates: All exported functions must have at least a basic TSDoc/JSDoc comment. When refactoring files (e.g., converting .js to .ts), verify that existing JSDoc comments on exported functions have not been accidentally removed in the process.

Do not merge code that retains unresolved inline comments whose purpose is pending verification (e.g., 'check with X before removing'). Resolve the question and either remove the comment or convert it to proper TSDoc before the MR is merged.

When implementing a feature that detects whether a browser built-in API is available at runtime (e.g., `if (Intl.Segmenter)`), add unit tests that stub out the API as `undefined` using `vi.stubGlobal` to cover the fallback code path, ensuring cross-browser behaviour is verified without requiring a real alternative browser.

When writing a `describe` or `it` block that specifically exercises the behaviour of a browser-compatibility fallback, add a comment explaining which browser lacks support for the feature and link to the relevant bug report or specification discussion.

When calling `Intl` APIs without an explicit locale (e.g., `new Intl.Segmenter(undefined, ...)`), add a code comment noting that the function's output may vary across environments or default locales, and cite the relevant spec rationale if locale-sensitivity is non-obvious.

When defining a function type alias (or callback type) whose return value is a boolean predicate, include a TSDoc comment that explicitly states which boolean value represents the positive/success case (e.g., `/** Returns true if the line fits the constraint */`).
